Methodology — calls & theses

Every call and thesis is a live formula of the current data. Change a peak, POS, or market cap and the direction, valuation, and thesis all update automatically — nothing here is hard-coded.

Call grid — valuation × science

Valuation = MC / fNPV (1.0 = fair). Science = (efficacy signal + differentiation) / 2. Weak <2.5 · Solid 2.5–3.5 · Strong ≥3.5. Weak science overrides cheapness (the value-trap guard).

MC/fNPV ↓   Science →Weak <2.5Solid 2.5–3.5Strong ≥3.5
Deep <0.33AVOIDLONGSTRONG BUY
Cheap 0.33–0.66AVOIDLONGLONG
Fair 0.66–1.5AVOIDHOLDWATCH
Rich 1.5–3.0SHORTSHORTWATCH
Very rich ≥3.0STRONG SHORTSTRONG SHORTSHORT

WATCH = strong asset but not cheap (watch for an entry). AVOID = broken/weak science regardless of price (a value trap when it screens cheap).

Thesis format

Each thesis is generated to one spine:

[CALL]. [drug — strongest efficacy stat, with its endpoint named]; [$ market cap vs $ prob-adj peak and $ fNPV], [catalyst + date] the catalyst. Falsifier: [the one thing that breaks it].

Valuation is shown in dollars across three anchors — market cap, probability-adjusted peak sales (peak × POS), and fNPV (3× prob-adj peak, time-discounted) — so the gap is legible without ratios.

Peak & POS re-rating

POS anchors to published stage→approval base rates (Preclinical ~6% → Ph3 ~50% → Filed ~85% → Approved ~97%), adjusted by efficacy signal, differentiation, and hard events parsed from each asset's own data (missed/failed/CRL cut it; met-primary/FDA-aligned/breakthrough lift it), then blended with the prior analyst POS and clamped to defensible stage bounds.

Peak sales are only ever trimmed, never inflated: penetration is capped by prevalence tier, price by modality, and an absolute stage-scaled ceiling removes indefensible outliers so the risk-adjusted value — and the upside/downside gap — is trustworthy.
